subject: Is there a way to create a copy of a Simulation Environment variable?

messages.author: e64b7f6e6af96a3e
messages.subject: Is there a way to create a copy of a Simulation Environment variable?
parts:
Hi,

I just started using Simmer. I was wondering if there is a way to make a copy of a Simulation environment variable?

The reason I would like to do this is because I am running a historic simulation that takes a few minutes (say stop time is 50), and then I would like to test different forecasting scenarios from time 50 to 58 which are much quicker. I wouldn’t want to re-run the full simulation every time I change forecasting parameters affecting period 50-58, I would like to run just from time 50 to 58. 

I was thinking that maybe I could just start each scenario by copying the historic simulation environment already run until time 50, so each time I change parameters and run it until time 58, I do not lose my original run until time 50.

To make a copy of the simulation environment I tried a simple leftward assignment:
Env_scen1 <- Env_hist

However, it results in a link to the same object. So when I advance the simulation on Env_scen1, it advances it on Env_hist too.

Thank you!
Luis

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Is there a way to create a copy of a Simulation Environment variable?
parts:
On Sat, 26 Feb 2022 at 00:09, Luis Acosta <acos...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,

I just started using Simmer. I was wondering if there is a way to make a copy of a Simulation environment variable?

The reason I would like to do this is because I am running a historic simulation that takes a few minutes (say stop time is 50), and then I would like to test different forecasting scenarios from time 50 to 58 which are much quicker. I wouldn’t want to re-run the full simulation every time I change forecasting parameters affecting period 50-58, I would like to run just from time 50 to 58. 

I was thinking that maybe I could just start each scenario by copying the historic simulation environment already run until time 50, so each time I change parameters and run it until time 58, I do not lose my original run until time 50.

To make a copy of the simulation environment I tried a simple leftward assignment:
Env_scen1 <- Env_hist

However, it results in a link to the same object. So when I advance the simulation on Env_scen1, it advances it on Env_hist too.

The simulation environment is a C++ object under the hood, so yes, assigning it to another variable just copies the reference to the same object. Unfortunately, currently there's no way to deep-copy a simulation (you can use the wrap method to just copy the results, but not the state, and a wrapped simulation is not runnable anymore). I agree this is an interesting feature, which requires the ability to (un)serialize, and more generally would allow us e.g. to save it to disk and restore it in another process or machine. But this is not a trivial problem and currently there's no roadmap for it.

What you can do is to run your simulations in parallel. It may take a few minutes to reach t=50. But then, it takes the same amount of time for n processes to reach the same point separately, and from there, they could diverge in different scenarios.

--
Iñaki Úcar

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Is there a way to create a copy of a Simulation Environment variable?
parts:
Thank you Iñaki! That’s could actually be a good workaround. I could pre-run several copies of the same simulation, have them ready for scenario forecasting when needed. I have not tried parallel in R in my machine yet, but I will do.

I can see that saving/restoring simulations is not trivial. Anyway, this platform has been very helpful for my project so far, look forward to future developments.

Cheers!
Luis

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Is there a way to create a copy of a Simulation Environment variable?
parts:
Hi,

Thanks again for the suggestion. I parallelized the execution of my code using future.apply and the example on replication in the website (introduction to simmer) until time 50.

It runs ok, I did it for 10 replications. However I realized the individual runs need to be wrapped, which as you mentioned, keep the results but not the states, so still I cannot use them as restart points to later run scenarios from time 50 to 58.

Am I missing something? Is there a way to run the simulations in parallel and get links to each environment without wrapping them?

Thank you,
Luis

Apologies, I probably wasn't clear enough. I was proposing wrapping the whole simulation into a function like this:

  # set parameters for scenario i

}

then parallelize the execution of that function.
